findings.reason: the plan's §6 text rests on "the reader reads each rule's source_group/source_array straight from the cache", and naming the extension of the view instead removes a second resolver the plan currently creates.
findings.text: `read_signal_map_observation` re-implements the rule→source-channel lookup (`rule.source_group`/`rule.source_array` → read) that `imas_ambix/data/virtual_zarr.py:130` `VirtualZarrView.__getitem__` already owns, so the mapping from a compiled rule to its raw array now has two owners that can drift; the plan justifies not reading *through* the view (it applies the assumed sign a `source-only` rule carries) but never considers the honest change, which is to give `VirtualZarrView` an untransformed accessor and read through it

— the packaged `units: {A, T, Wb}` table is a third place unit spellings live beside the signal-map rules' own per-rule `source_unit`/`target_unit` and the DD unit vocabulary `jtmm-unit-audit` reads from imas-python, and its only reader is `tests/data/test_jt60sa_signal_maps.py:38` — no runtime path loads it; WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: no — REASON: it is a landed, test-only identity table whose removal is a cleanup, not a design change, so it does not alter the plan's architecture.

response_events.reason: the EDDB unit table is test-only by design: section 5 resolves each EDDB spelling when a binding is authored, never at run time, so its test is its intended consumer and the per-rule source_unit stays the runtime owner

duplicate_owner-2.reason: the EDDB unit table is test-only by design: section 5 resolves each EDDB spelling when a binding is authored, never at run time, so its test is its intended consumer and the per-rule source_unit stays the runtime owner

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new public surfaces are few and deep: `read_signal_map_observation` and `measure_convention` each hide the raw/equilibrium join and the Grad–Shafranov scoring behind one signature, and the EQDB transport/record/writer extend `eddb_remote.py` and `eddb.py` rather than fanning out into per-concern wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §6 observation reader resolves a signal-map rule to its raw channel itself, duplicating the resolution `VirtualZarrView.__getitem__` already owns; one further instance (the packaged EDDB unit table) is a duplicate vocabulary with no production consumer.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; each design section that adds public surface states in its own text what it retires or why nothing can (§2 adds one exporter function and retires nothing because no exporter exists; §6 retires `read_catalogue_observation` and adds `read_signal_map_observation`, adds two EQDB types retiring nothing; §7 retires `PINNED_SEMANTIC_IDENTITY`/`PINNED_PHYSICAL_DIGEST`/`PINNED_REGISTRY_DIGEST` and their re-export while adding the machine-keyed pin table and the JT-60SA shot set).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every prospective change names the mechanism it extends and the owner exists in the tree (§6 reuses `gs/operator.py` `build_operator`/`vacuum_prediction`/`assemble_pf_currents`, `eddb.read_channel`, `cocos_convention.score_convention`; §7 reuses `eval/efit_referee.py` `judge_geometry`/`read_efit_geometry` and `gs/machine_identity.py` `default_registry`/`identity_for_shot`), and where the plan adds a format (tokamap) or transport (EQDB) it states why no owner can be extended.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — where the plan adds a layer it says why the existing machinery cannot serve it (VirtualZarrView applies a compiled transform it must not apply; the tokamap exporter has no existing owner; the EQDB request/record are not channel-shaped). The one place that rejection was argued rather than the extension considered is filed below as a duplicate owner.
